description: 5 exemplars + 3 near-misses + 2 counterexamples. Authored 2026-10-01 under road-to-corpus-refresh-cadence-shape 1.2a, which touched this skill's grounding corpus and so brought it into check_routing_coverage's touched-skill scope. Exemplars cover the audit request in its explicit and implicit forms, including the German phrasing the skill's own description names. Near-misses are three neighbours that share vocabulary with an a11y audit and are still somebody else's job: token-level contrast fixes and structural landmark/heading fixes, which this skill's SKILL.md names explicitly (tailwind-engineer, ui-component-architect), plus component inventory (existing-ui-audit), which it does not name and which is included because it runs first over the same components. Counterexamples guard the 'accessible' homonym (permissions, not WCAG) and routine design-system work that mentions UI without asking anything of it.

queries.q: review this screen for accessibility before we ship it
is this modal usable with the keyboard only, and does focus return where it should?
a user on a screen reader says our combobox announces nothing — audit it
does this form meet WCAG 2.2 AA?
mach das Formular barrierefrei — Tastaturbedienung und Screenreader bitte prüfen
our contrast tokens are too light — fix the palette values in the Tailwind config
queries.note: shares the contrast vocabulary, but this is a token-level fix in the design system rather than an audit verdict → tailwind-engineer, which this skill's SKILL.md names for exactly this

queries.q: the landmarks and heading order in this layout are wrong — restructure the component tree
queries.note: the sharpest edge: landmarks and heading order are a11y findings, but the ask is the structural fix, not the finding → ui-component-architect, also named in this skill's SKILL.md

queries.q: which button and input variants do we already have before I add another one?
queries.note: a UI inventory over the same components, with no standard to audit against → existing-ui-audit. Not named in this skill's SKILL.md, unlike the two near-misses above; included because it runs first over the same surface

queries.q: make the staging dashboard accessible to the QA team
queries.note: the 'accessible' homonym — permissions and reachability, not WCAG. Guards against triggering on the word rather than the subject

queries.q: write the release notes for v4 of the design system
queries.note: routine UI-adjacent work that names components and asks nothing about how they behave for anyone
